labs.scope.qualitative: Qualitative teaching model: compare the selected reagents. Reaction speed, yield and concentration are not predicted.
labs.scope.rays: Qualitative ray paths; fields and trajectories are schematic, not calibrated. Paddle motion alone is not conclusive evidence of particle momentum.
labs.scope.geometry: Projected spatial model with bonded neighbours and lone pairs. Colours, distances and angles are schematic; bond order and resonance are not drawn.
labs.scope.balance: Inspect glassware and balance a known practice mass by adjusting the combined rider mass after loading. This is a mass-balance model, not a calibrated four-beam instrument.
labs.scope.gas_readings: Measured-data practice: replace the example readings with your own. Correct wet gas pressure using the handbook table, then calculate the result. Gas generation and leakage are not predicted.
labs.scope.calorimetry: Compare equal acid/base portions using synthetic practice temperatures or your entered readings. Heat capacity is approximated by water; heat loss and cup heat capacity are neglected.
labs.scope.hess: Compare A+B with C+D using practice data or entered temperature rises. Solution density and heat capacity are approximated by water. Real data need not give exact agreement.
labs.scope.flame: Qualitative flame colours. Display colours depend on your screen and are not spectra or measurements.
labs.scope.anions: Selected confirmatory reactions; use fresh portions and the reagent listed in the method. This is not an unknown-mixture separation model.
labs.scope.nitrogen: Magnesium nitride formation and its hydrolysis are modelled qualitatively. Heating and cooling use virtual time; product composition is not calculated.
labs.scope.halides: Selected silver-halide/ammonia and chlorine-displacement tests. The handbook lead-salt branch is not modelled here. No partition coefficient or excess-chlorine chemistry is predicted.
labs.scope.titration_readings: Endpoint and calculation practice using entered burette readings. Example titres are not NIE results. This model does not predict an unknown concentration or simulate continuous drop delivery.
labs.scope.solubility: Compare the NIE table classifications: soluble, sparingly soluble and insoluble. Concentration-dependent precipitation and solubility products are not calculated.
labs.scope.thermal: Compare theoretical thermal products under sufficient heating. Decomposition temperatures differ greatly; a laboratory flame will not decompose every listed carbonate. Heating time and temperature are not simulated.
labs.scope.aqueous: Idealised aqueous-ion colours. Ligands, concentration, oxidation and hydration can change a real solution’s colour; these changes are not modelled.
labs.error.invalid_input: Enter finite readings within the displayed limits. Gas temperature must be tabulated; mass loss, dry pressure and titre must be positive.
labs.error.safety_required: Read and acknowledge the precautions first.
labs.error.wrong_order: Follow the procedure in order. Start a new trial to change the sample.
labs.error.no_result: Complete and record the required trials first.
labs.error.stale_sequence: The action used an outdated state. Try the current control again.
labs.error.unsupported: This model version is not supported.
labs.error.dangerous_combination: Sodium with dilute acid is blocked as a dangerous combination.
labs.error.inconsistent_trials: The last three titres must differ by less than 0.1 cm³. Record further trials.
labs.observation.rays_straight: Cathode rays travel in straight lines toward the fluorescent screen.
labs.observation.rays_shadow: The opaque cross blocks rays and casts a shadow on the fluorescent screen.
labs.observation.rays_paddle: The wheel moves. Heating can also cause motion, so this observation alone does not establish particle momentum.
labs.observation.rays_up: The negatively charged beam deflects toward the positive upper plate.
labs.observation.rays_down: The negatively charged beam deflects toward the positive lower plate.
labs.observation.rays_magnetic: A magnetic field deflects the beam perpendicular to the field; the drawn path is qualitative.
labs.observation.molecule_model: Compare bonded neighbours and lone pairs with the displayed spatial model.
labs.observation.balance_equal: The known mass and combined rider mass balance.
labs.observation.balance_heavy: The sample side is heavier. Increase the rider mass.
labs.observation.balance_light: The rider side is heavier. Decrease the rider mass.
labs.observation.oxygen_collected: Use the entered mass loss and dry, corrected gas volume to determine molar volume.
labs.observation.hydrogen_collected: Use dry hydrogen pressure, volume and temperature to determine the molar mass of magnesium.
labs.observation.calorimetry_readings: Calculate heat gained by the solution and the corresponding molar reaction enthalpy.
labs.observation.hess_comparison: Compare H₁ + H₂ with H₃ + H₄. A nonzero difference can reflect experimental heat loss or measurement error.
labs.observation.metal_oxidation: An oxide layer forms in air; the metal and conditions affect the rate and appearance.
labs.observation.magnesium_cold: Magnesium reacts very slowly with cold water; little visible change is expected.
labs.observation.magnesium_hot: Heating increases magnesium’s reaction with water; hydrogen is released.
labs.observation.sodium_water: Sodium reacts vigorously with water, forming an alkaline solution and hydrogen.
labs.observation.metal_hydrogen: Hydrogen is evolved as the metal reacts with the selected medium.
labs.observation.flame_lilac: Potassium: lilac flame; sodium contamination can mask it.
labs.observation.flame_none: Magnesium salts give no characteristic visible flame colour in this test.
labs.observation.sulfate: Acidified barium test: a white sulfate precipitate persists in dilute acid.
labs.observation.sulfite: Acid releases sulfur dioxide, which turns acidified dichromate from orange to green.
labs.observation.sulfide: Lead acetate gives a black sulfide precipitate.
labs.observation.thiosulfate: Dilute acid produces cloudy sulfur and sulfur dioxide.
labs.observation.nitrate: The carefully layered iron(II)/sulfuric acid test gives a brown ring at the interface.
labs.observation.nitrite: Acidification releases brown nitrogen dioxide-containing fumes.
labs.observation.carbonate: Acid releases carbon dioxide: limewater turns milky; excess gas can clear it.
labs.observation.nessler_brown: Nessler reagent gives a brown coloration or precipitate with ammonia/ammonium in alkaline conditions.
labs.observation.litmus_blue: Ammonia turns damp red litmus blue.
labs.observation.silver_dissolves: The silver-halide precipitate dissolves in the selected ammonia solution.
labs.observation.silver_bromide: Pale-yellow silver bromide remains in dilute ammonia; concentrated ammonia dissolves it.
labs.observation.silver_iodide: Yellow silver iodide remains insoluble in dilute and concentrated ammonia.
labs.observation.halide_no_displacement: Chlorine does not displace chloride; no new halogen is produced.
labs.observation.bromine_layer: Chlorine displaces bromine; the organic layer is orange-brown.
labs.observation.iodine_layer: Chlorine displaces iodine; the organic layer is violet. Excess chlorine is outside this model.
labs.observation.starch_colourless: Near the endpoint, starch makes the iodine mixture blue; thiosulfate removes iodine until the blue disappears.
labs.observation.permanent_pink: The endpoint is a faint pink colour persisting for the prescribed interval; use the entered titre in the calculation.
labs.observation.ammonium_no_gas: Aqueous ammonium chloride alone does not release ammonia for the HCl-rod test; alkali is required.
labs.observation.ammonia_fumes: Ammonia and hydrogen chloride form white ammonium chloride fumes.
labs.observation.ammonium_acidic: Ammonium chloride solution is acidic. Damp red litmus stays red; this is not a positive ammonia gas test.
labs.observation.solubility_SS: NIE table: sparingly soluble. Visible precipitation depends on concentrations, which are not modelled.
labs.observation.solubility_IS: NIE table: insoluble; a precipitate is expected under suitable test conditions.
labs.observation.carbonate_stable: Sodium and potassium carbonates are stable under ordinary laboratory heating.
labs.observation.carbonate_carbon_dioxid: Under sufficient heating, decomposition releases carbon dioxide, which turns limewater milky. Required temperatures vary by salt.
labs.observation.nitrate_oxygen: Sodium/potassium nitrate decomposes to nitrite and oxygen on heating; oxygen relights a glowing splint.
labs.observation.nitrate_nitrogen_dioxid: Group 2 nitrates form the oxide, brown nitrogen dioxide and oxygen under sufficient heating.
labs.observation.aqua_violet: Idealised chromium(III) aqua ion: blue-violet; other coordinated species can look green.
labs.observation.aqua_yellow_brown: Iron(III): yellow-brown under ordinary aqueous conditions.
labs.method.1: Choose the tube arrangement, connect its circuit, energize, observe, then switch off. Reverse electric plate polarity to compare deflection.
labs.method.2: Select a molecule or ion, identify its modelled atom, assemble bonded neighbours and inspect the geometry. For diatomic molecules, one end is the modelled atom.
labs.method.3: Inspect the chosen glassware, zero the empty balance, load a known mass, then adjust the rider total to balance it. Volumetric flask: fixed-volume solution; pipette: fixed aliquot; burette: variable delivered volume; beaker: approximate volume; funnel: transfer; watch glass: weighing support.
labs.method.5: Collect oxygen over water while heating potassium chlorate with catalyst. Weigh before and after cooling. Equalize water levels. Subtract water-vapour pressure; correct volume to STP and divide by moles from oxygen mass loss.
labs.method.6: React a weighed magnesium ribbon with excess dilute acid. Collect hydrogen over water, equalize levels and correct for water vapour. Use PV = nRT and the 1:1 magnesium-to-hydrogen ratio. Repeat three times.
labs.method.7: Mix 50 cm³ acid and 50 cm³ base, each 2 mol dm⁻³. Average the initial temperatures and record the maximum after mixing. Use total solution mass 100 g, heat capacity 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹ and reacting amount 0.1 mol.
labs.method.8: Compare dissolving solid NaOH followed by neutralization (A+B) against acid dilution followed by solid addition (C+D). Use the handbook 0.25 mol basis, solution masses 125 g for A and 250 g for B/C/D, and heat capacity 4.2 J g⁻¹ K⁻¹.
labs.method.9: Compare small sodium, magnesium and calcium samples in air, cold/hot water or dilute acid. Sodium with acid is blocked. Observe oxidation or hydrogen formation.
labs.method.10: Clean the flame-test wire, moisten with hydrochloric acid, take the salt and place it in the non-luminous flame. Compare colours using a fresh, clean wire for each sample.
labs.method.11: Use fresh portions: sulfate—acidified barium test; sulfite—dilute acid and acidified dichromate gas test; sulfide—lead acetate; thiosulfate—dilute acid; nitrate—iron(II) followed by carefully layered concentrated sulfuric acid; nitrite—acidification; carbonate—dilute acid with limewater gas test.
labs.method.12: Heat cleaned magnesium in a covered crucible; cool before adding water. Hydrolysis of the nitride product releases ammonia, tested with damp red litmus or Nessler reagent.
labs.method.13: On fresh portions, acidify with dilute nitric acid and add silver nitrate, then test with the chosen ammonia concentration. Alternatively add chlorine water and compare the chloroform layer for displaced halogen.
labs.method.14: Acidify 25 cm³ standard iodate and add excess iodide. Titrate liberated iodine with thiosulfate to pale yellow, add starch, then continue until blue disappears. Repeat trials; use the 1:6 iodate-to-thiosulfate ratio.
labs.method.15: Compare aqueous ammonia with ammonium chloride, with or without added alkali. Use damp red litmus, the hydrochloric-acid rod test or Nessler reagent; do not smell the gas.
labs.method.16: Choose a potassium or group-2 cation, add the anion solution dropwise and compare with NIE Resource Book Table 4.5. Sparingly soluble is a separate classification from insoluble.
labs.method.17: Compare thermal products of the selected carbonate, bicarbonate or nitrate. Test evolved gases with limewater or a glowing splint as appropriate. Remove delivery tubing from liquid before stopping heat to prevent suck-back.
labs.method.18: Dissolve the prescribed small salt sample in distilled water and compare aqueous metal-ion colours. Use the idealised ion chart; real coordination chemistry may alter colour.
labs.method.19: Prepare the ferrous solution, take 25 cm³, add the prescribed acid mixture and titrate with standard permanganate. Confirm a faint pink endpoint for 30 seconds. Use five iron(II) ions per permanganate ion.
labs.method.20: Take 25 cm³ standard oxalate, acidify and warm as prescribed. Titrate with permanganate to a faint pink colour persisting for 30 seconds. The balanced mole ratio is two permanganate to five oxalate.
labs.precaution.1: High-voltage tubes must only be handled by a qualified teacher; switch off before changing connections.
labs.precaution.2: Use molecular models safely; the colours and sizes are conventions.
labs.precaution.3: Handle glassware carefully and keep the balance pan clean and dry.
labs.precaution.5: Oxidizer and heating hazard: use small quantities, eye protection and teacher supervision. Avoid suck-back and never heat a sealed system.
labs.precaution.6: Hydrogen is flammable; keep away from flames. Use dilute acid and eye protection.
labs.precaution.7: Acids and alkalis are corrosive. Wear eye protection and add reagents carefully.
labs.precaution.8: Dissolving alkali and acid dilution release heat. Wear eye protection; handle solid alkali with tools.
labs.precaution.9: Sodium, hydrogen and hot water pose fire/burn hazards. Sodium reactions require teacher control. Sodium with acid is blocked.
labs.precaution.10: Flames, acid and hot wire can burn. Some salts are toxic; never taste them.
labs.precaution.11: Toxic gases, lead/chromium reagents and concentrated acid require teacher supervision and suitable ventilation. Never smell gases directly.
labs.precaution.12: Do not look directly at burning magnesium. Cool the crucible before adding water; ammonia and Nessler reagent require controlled handling.
labs.precaution.13: Halogens, chloroform, silver salts and ammonia require supervised handling and appropriate waste collection.
labs.precaution.14: Avoid iodine contact and acid splashes. Never mouth-pipette.
labs.precaution.15: Ammonia and hydrogen chloride irritate the respiratory system. Nessler reagent is hazardous; use ventilation and supervised disposal.
labs.precaution.16: Barium and chromate reagents can be toxic. Collect chemical waste separately.
labs.precaution.17: Nitrogen dioxide is toxic. Use supervised ventilation, heat-resistant equipment and disconnect gas tubing before stopping heat.
labs.precaution.18: Metal salts can be harmful; avoid contact and collect waste separately.
labs.precaution.19: Permanganate is an oxidizer; the acid mixture is corrosive. Never mouth-pipette.
labs.precaution.20: Hot acidified oxalate and permanganate require eye protection and supervised handling. Never mouth-pipette.
